programme.title: Da Vinci: The Lost Treasure
programme.desc: Fiona Bruce uncovers the story of Leonardo da Vinci, who is considered by many to be one of the greatest artists who ever lived. Yet his reputation rests on only a handful of pictures - including the world's most famous painting, the `Mona Lisa'. Fiona travels to Florence, Milan, Paris and Warsaw to learn more about this enigmatic genius - and to New York, where she's given a preview of a new Leonardo work.

programme.title: Planet Earth
programme.desc: David Attenborough narrates the epic journey of a humpback whale and calf as they cross the richest seas that fringe the coasts. From tropical paradises, where the newborn calf takes his first faltering breaths, to the storm-ravaged icy polar seas, the whales' great feeding grounds, seas of great contrast and surprise are revealed.

programme.title: Face the Music
programme.desc: Joseph Cooper invites viewers to match their musical wits against Joyce Grenfell, Richard Baker and David Attenborough. With guest musician Andrew Davis.

programme.title: The Biddy Baxter Story
programme.desc: Profile of the legendary `Blue Peter' editor Biddy Baxter, with contributions from Sarah Greene, Valerie Singleton, Simon Groom and Peter Purves. Includes clips from `Blue Peter'. Presented by Sarah Dunant.

programme.title: Planet Earth
programme.desc: David Attenborough reveals the greatest woodlands on earth, from the evergreen forests of the frozen north to the deciduous dry forests of the equator. The Taiga forest is a silent world of stunted conifers cloaked in snow and ice. By contrast, the broadleaf forests of North America and Europe bustle with life, while the baobab forests of Madagascar are the strangest of all, with bizarre upside-down trees.

programme.title: The Good Life
programme.desc: When drought wreaks havoc with the Goods' agricultural plans, the Leadbetters try to revive their neighbours' spirits.

programme.title: Yes, Minister
programme.desc: Jim encounters problems when he is given responsibility for developing and implementing an integrated national transport policy.

programme.title: Rikki
programme.desc: A centenary celebration of the life and legacy of Rikki Fulton, one of Scotland's most beloved comic actors. Ashley Jensen narrates an affectionate tribute to one of Scotland's funniest comedians, Rikki Fulton. It's 100 years since Rikki first made an entrance on to the world stage and 20 years since he bowed out. For decades he's been making the nation laugh with his rubber face, razor sharp wit and laconic demeanour.

programme.title: Scotch and Wry
programme.desc: Hogmanay comedy from Rikki Fulton, Gregor Fisher, Juliet Cadzow, Tony Roper, Annette Staines and Barbara Dickson.

programme.title: The Last Battle of the Vikings
programme.desc: Marine archeologist Dr Jon Henderson tells the incredible story of the Norsemen in Scotland. Visiting fascinating archeological sites across Scotland and Norway, he reveals that, although the battle at Largs marked the end of an era for the Norsemen, their presence continued to shape the identity and culture of the Scottish nation to the present day.

programme.title: The Lost Neanderthals
programme.desc: The Mandrin Cave in southern France has been attracting the attention of archaeologists for 30 years. The cave was regularly occupied in prehistoric times, and a remarkable record of human habitation has been preserved by its soils.

programme.title: A Timewatch Guide
programme.desc: Historian Dan Snow explores the greatest maritime archaeology project in British history, the Mary Rose. Using 40 years of BBC archive footage Dan charts how the Mary Rose was discovered, excavated and eventually raised, and what the latest research has revealed about this iconic ship and her crew. Dan also investigates how the Mary Rose project helped create modern underwater archaeology, examining the techniques, challenges and triumphs of the divers and archaeologists involved.

programme.title: Planet Earth
programme.desc: David Attenborough takes a look at life deep undersea. A 30-tonne whale shark gorges on a school of fish and a unique overhead camera reveals the speed of common dolphins. Descending into the abyss, deep sea octopus fly with wings and vampire squid use bioluminescence to create a colour display. Time-lapse footage from 2,000m down captures eels, crabs and giant isopods eating.

programme.title: Britain's Nuclear Secrets: Inside Sellafield
programme.desc: Nuclear physicist Professor Jim Al-Khalili uncovers the story of Sellafield. He encounters some of the most dangerous substances on earth, reveals the nature of radiation and even attempts to split the atom.

programme.title: Tribe
programme.desc: While living with the Sanema people of the Venezuelan Amazon, Bruce Parry takes part in a shamanistic festival.

programme.title: Witness for the Prosecution
programme.desc: A top-flight barrister attempts to defend murder suspect Leonard Vole, who stands accused of murdering a wealthy widow for the fortune she left behind. To make matters worse, his alibi, provided by his wife Christine, falls down when it is revealed their marriage is not fully legal and she can be used as a witness for the prosecution.

programme.title: The Sky at Night
programme.desc: The team explores one of the greatest discoveries of modern astronomy that our universe is expanding, and the new questions it raises about how the cosmos works. Maggie Aderin-Pocock investigates a different cosmic speedometer.

programme.title: Earth's Natural Wonders
programme.desc: In the high Himalaya, join yak-herder Thokmay Lowa and his small group as he steers his herd through one of the region's extreme mountain passes. In the Canadian Arctic, 63-year-old Minnie Nappaaluk and her granddaughter Eva embark on one of the most hazardous expeditions for food: the mussel harvest. In the blistering Australian outback, the only way to efficiently round up cattle herds on vast farms is through the use of helicopter cowboys like Chris Weyand.

programme.title: Gentlemen Prefer Blondes
programme.desc: Showgirl Lorelei and best friend Dorothy embark upon a boat trip to Paris, where Lorelei intends to marry millionaire Gus Esmond. En route, the girls are bedevilled by private detective Malone, hired by Esmond's father to make certain that Lorelei isn't just another gold-digger. When Dorothy falls in love with the poverty-stricken Malone, Lorelei decides to find her pal a wealthier potential husband.

programme.title: Parkinson
programme.sub-title: Harry Secombe, Harold Robbins and Anita Loos
programme.desc: Michael Parkinson chats to Harry Secombe, Harold Robbins and Anita Loos.

programme.title: Dunkirk
programme.desc: A dramatic reconstruction of the World War II rout at Dunkirk. The Allied defeat and the subsequent frantic evacuation is told through the experiences of three different characters: a cockney corporal and his men separated from their unit; a newspaper reporter who moves from cool detachment to being willing to lay down his life; and a civilian whose eyes are opened by the dramatic events.

programme.title: Talking Pictures
programme.desc: A retrospective look at television appearances made over the years by the Oscar-winning actor Sir John Mills, capturing the milestones and highlights of his life and career.
